segmentation.text: shall not bring a vehicle to a complete stop
so as to impede or block the normal and reasonable movement of

elements.justification: Reuses the index mapping of 'A person' (LVMC_11_22_010): the person who brings a vehicle to a stop is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the class is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, 'membership of a legal aggregate', not the role of driving.

A complete stop is the concept drv.motion.complete_halt: 'The road user is at rest at the observation — "complete cessation from movement" — observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance the caller sets', filled with p.halt_speed_tolerance. Of the two stop definitions the run leaves ambiguous, DEF-NRS-484A-255 ('complete cessation from movement') and DEF-NRS-484A-260 ('any halting, even momentarily'), both denote this halt; the concept says nothing of how long the vehicle stays at rest, so a momentary halt is read too. 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

Upon a roadway: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', which is DEF-NRS-484A-220 ('improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder'); 'Not a stand-in for: the sidewalk' — a halt on the shoulder or in a bay is not on the roadway.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'); the traffic whose movement is impeded is a traffic road user behind the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) at a body gap (rel.surface_gap) the operationalization of x4 bounds.

Safe operation requires the stop where the subject halts behind a road user ahead of it in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within a queue gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap), or where some road user is predicted to come close to it (prim.closest_approach_within, prim.closest_approach_distance; 'Not a stand-in for ... the danger of a crash' alone, the bound being the operationalization of x6).

Extends the index mapping of 'or in compliance with law' (NRS_484B_450_1a: dev.governs, dev.stop_sign, dev.traffic_signal, rel.occupies, st.travel_region) with the other controls whose indication requires a halt, as the mapping of 'shall not: Stop, stand or park a vehicle' (NRS_484B_477_1a) reads them: a stop sign (dev.stop_sign, 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt'), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign, 'requiring yielding without a mandatory halt', where a halt is how the yield is given), a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), a person directing traffic with indication stop (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard or railroad_flagger), or railway lights flashing or a gate not up (dev.railway_signal_or_gate), governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position', and no position is read from it.

operationalizations.standard: so as to impede or block the normal and reasonable movement of traffic
operationalizations.convention: Queue convention: the halt impedes or blocks traffic where a traffic road user is behind the halted subject in the same lane with the gap between bodies within p.rear_signal_reach (immediately to the rear) and that road user is itself at rest (complete halt within p.halt_speed_tolerance: blocked) or decelerating at p.speed_decrease_decel_min or more (impeded).

operationalizations.standard: the stop is necessary for safe operation
operationalizations.convention: Queue spacing and the traffic-conflict technique: the stop is necessary where a road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane with the body gap within p.queue_halt_gap (the subject halts behind other traffic), or where some road user's centre is predicted to come within p.conflict_centre_clearance of the subject's within p.conflict_horizon.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) occupying a roadway.
obligation: Violated where the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) and some traffic road user other than the subject is behind it in the same lane with the body gap within p.rear_signal_reach and is at rest or decelerating at p.speed_decrease_decel_min or more; except where (a) some road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane with the body gap within p.queue_halt_gap, or some road user's closest approach to the subject lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or (b) a control requiring a halt governs a travel region the subject occupies: a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, a person directing traffic with indication stop, or railway crossing lights flashing or a gate not up. A moving subject, or one halted with no traffic held behind it, complies.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who brings the vehicle to a stop is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
'the normal and reasonable movement of traffic' is read only through traffic behind the subject in its own lane, halted or decelerating; traffic in other lanes is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car halts mid-block in a roadway lane with no road user ahead, no road user in predicted conflict and no stop sign or signal; a car behind it in the same lane halts 4 m behind.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same halt, but a bus is halted 3 m ahead of the car in its lane: the car halts behind other traffic.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car halts in a parking space off the roadway with a car passing behind it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not supply the in-lane ahead/behind relation, so neither the follower held behind nor the absence of a vehicle ahead is observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a stop sign governs the lane the car occupies.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car halts in a roadway lane with no other road user in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.rear_signal_reach
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies within which a following vehicle in the same lane is immediately to the rear of a vehicle: two seconds of headway at an urban speed of about 15 m/s
param_proposals.source: two-second headway rule of driver manuals

param_proposals.name: p.speed_decrease_decel_min
param_proposals.convention: the longitudinal deceleration at or beyond which a sampled acceleration counts as a decrease of speed rather than noise or rolling resistance: the acceleration resolution of the source

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source

param_proposals.name: p.queue_halt_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies to a road user ahead in the same lane within which a halt is a halt behind other traffic: the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue
param_proposals.source: queue spacing of halted vehicles (jam density)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
